question: in molecules with triple bonds, how many of them are not carcinogenic?
evidence: triple bond refers to bond_type = '#'; label = '-' means molecules are non-carcinogenic
clarification: Count every row, including repeated molecule_id values.
gold: SELECT COUNT(T1.molecule_id) FROM molecule AS T1 INNER JOIN bond AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T2.bond_type = '#' AND T1.label = '-'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.molecule_id) FROM molecule AS T1 INNER JOIN bond AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T2.bond_type = '#' AND T1.label = '-'

d.request: Among molecules with triple bonds (bond_type = '#'), how many are non-carcinogenic (label = '-')? Count every row, including repeated molecule_id values, rather than only distinct molecules.
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(m.molecule_id) FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#' AND m.label = '-'

c.request:
in molecules with triple bonds, how many of them are not carcinogenic?

b.request: Counting every row (including repeated molecule_id values) from joining molecule and bond, how many rows have bond_type = '#' and molecule label = '-' (non-carcinogenic), without deduplicating molecules?
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM molecule AS m INNER JOIN bond AS b ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#' AND m.label = '-'
